I have been doing professional website development for the last 4 years. I had about 3 years of freelancing in the same field before that, and after the freelancing / before my current job, I helped run the marketing and sales department for one of the largest sellers on eBay.

AMA about web design, development, eBay, marketing, SEO, etc!

As someone who have done professional web-app development for over 20 years and development in general a few years longer, how do you think you'll develop your skillset in the future, what are you aiming for? Anything you know now will be outdated within a few years.

I've already come up against my knowledge being outdated; it's just the nature of the industry. I read news and discussions about web technology everyday to stay current, and make a point to work with emerging techniques and standards so that I'm always up on the latest practices.

In the distant future, say 10 - 15 years, the web will be sufficiently different that I think it's likely developers myself will cease to work with the front end, and will most likely assume back end roles, developing systems that themselves are used by the end user to create front end interfaces. We're already seeing this with things like Squarespace and Webflow.

Unless there's a drastic paradigm shift, there will always be a need for developers and programmers at some step in the process.

I think most website building and most (web)app development will be automated to a fair degree and it's something I've been developing for a long time. Traditional software development will only be required for writing custom modules into the automation suite itself. I think it's similar to how manual typesetting changed with desktop publishing and how calculators and computers replaced the computer-profession. This doesn't eliminate the developer profession more than computers replaced mathematicians, but the role will change, there will be more competition for excellence and it definitely won't be as common as a stand-alone profession it's now. Think about how almost everyone is a typist now (it used to be a specialized profession as well), and how everyone will be a developer in the future (with suitably powerful easy to use tools).

I agree, and it's something I'm okay with. The web is heading in a direction that focuses on content generation, with each user also being a potential source for content. This will naturally lead toward development of systems which make it easier to publish and distribute that content, which we're already seeing with things like Facebook, Twitter, or even Reddit (or Voat, for that matter).

I think the goal of any survival-minded developer would have to be to help create those systems. As in any industry, those who don't evolve with the times get pushed aside in favor of the survivors.
